sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: I have docked below at Interactive Lab 1: the Local Differential Privacy and NILM Cloaking Studio! Switch between Balanced Utility, High Privacy, and Low Privacy presets to see how reducing epsilon below 0.15 obscures appliance turn-on spikes in smart meter telemetry.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Watch that live perturbed wattage trace below! At Low Privacy epsilon 2.00, the microwave and water heater edges jump right out of the curve, whereas High Privacy epsilon 0.10 completely hides residential routines!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: I have docked below at Interactive Lab 2: the Chi-Square Sensor Spoofing Detection Studio! Select Adversarial Replay Attack above to watch abnormal low-bin concentration drive the Chi-square statistic far beyond the critical threshold.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at that red rejection zone on the right Chi-square distribution! The moment an adversarial script replays synthetic telemetry biased toward bins B0 and B1, the gateway quarantines the entire feed!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1! A smart water meter has sensitivity Delta f equal to 15.0 Liters and privacy budget epsilon equal to 0.50. Compute Laplace scale b, standard deviation sigma, and the variance multiplier if epsilon tightens to 0.10.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 1, Dr. Nova! Let's compute b equal to Delta f over epsilon, find sigma via root 2 times b, and check how tightening epsilon fivefold scales noise variance!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding deduction! Scale b equals 15 divided by 0.50, giving 30.0 Liters, and standard deviation equals 42.43 Liters. Because Laplace variance scales inversely with epsilon squared, tightening epsilon fivefold from 0.50 to 0.10 increases variance by 25 times!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Remember that Laplace scale b equals Delta f divided by epsilon, giving 30.0 Liters, and standard deviation is root 2 times 30.0 equals 42.43 Liters. Variance scales inversely with the square of epsilon, increasing 25-fold for a fivefold reduction in epsilon.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2! A security gateway bins vibration telemetry into B equals 16 frequency bands over a baseline batch of N equals 1,600 readings. Calculate the Chi-square degrees of freedom and expected count per bin.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 2! Sixteen histogram bins over 1,600 samples. Remember one degree of freedom is consumed by the fixed sample sum constraint!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! With 16 bins, degrees of freedom nu equals 16 minus 1 equals 15, and dividing 1,600 samples uniformly yields an expected count of 100.0 readings per bin. Any observed stream scoring Chi-square above 30.578 is quarantined!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. For B equals 16 frequency bins, degrees of freedom is B minus 1 equals 15. Dividing 1,600 total samples across 16 uniform bins gives 100.0 expected readings per bin.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3! A wearable PM2.5 monitor transmits K equals 720 hourly readings per month at epsilon zero equal to 0.05 per query. Compare linear sequential composition against advanced composition with delta equal to 10 to the minus 5.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Final checkpoint! Compare naive linear summation against Dwork and Abadi's square-root advanced composition across 720 monthly telemetry queries!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Masterful composition analysis! Naive sequential composition predicts epsilon equal to 36.0, whereas advanced composition evaluates to approximately 6.438 plus 1.846 equals 8.284—more than four times tighter!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Linear composition multiplies 720 queries by 0.05 to yield 36.0, whereas advanced composition uses the square root of 2 K natural log of 1 over delta, compressing the cumulative privacy loss down to 8.284.
